full_caption: Blackthorn Ridge Land & Timber Co., Appellant, v. Foxglove Landing Capital Servicing, LLC, Appellee
court: Kestrel Land and Property Court, Pinecrest Division
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: The Pinecrest County Redevelopment Authority condemned 8.9 acres owned by Foxglove Landing Capital Servicing, LLC at 4778 Harper's Cut, Pinecrest, KS for construction of a county recycling transfer station. The sole issue on appeal is the measure of just compensation.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: Just compensation is the fair market value of the property taken at the date of taking, measured by the price a willing buyer would pay a willing seller, neither being under compulsion.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: A taking may be effected without formal proceedings where governmental action substantially deprives the owner of the beneficial use of the land. The 6-month closure of the only access drive states a claim for inverse condemnation.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: The highest and best use of the property is the use to which it may reasonably be put in the reasonably near future. A use dependent on a rezoning is admissible only on a showing that the rezoning was reasonably probable.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: The 'scope of the project' rule excludes from the valuation any increase or decrease in value attributable to the project itself, including value changes flowing from the announcement of the project.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Evidence of the price paid by the condemnor for neighboring parcels is generally inadmissible, because such sales are made under the shadow of the condemnation power and are not free-market transactions.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Public use is satisfied where the taking serves a legitimate public purpose; the transfer of the condemned land to a private developer under an enforceable redevelopment agreement does not defeat that purpose under this State's constitution.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: The trial court excluded testimony valuing the parcel as light-industrial land. Given the pending comprehensive-plan amendment and three comparable rezonings in the corridor, the probability showing was made and the exclusion was error.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: Interest on the award runs from the date of taking to the date of payment at the statutory rate of 8 percent, and is a component of just compensation rather than a matter of legislative grace.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: Business losses are not compensable as such. Loss of goodwill is recoverable only where a statute so provides; this State's statute permits recovery of relocation expenses of $45,000 but not lost profits.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: Where only part of a parcel is taken, the owner recovers the value of the part taken plus severance damages to the remainder, less any special benefit conferred on the remainder by the project.

sections.heading: Paragraph 12
sections.text: The judgment is reversed and the cause remanded for a new trial on valuation with the excluded testimony admitted.

sections.heading: RIDER 2 — MEASURE OF JUST COMPENSATION
sections.text: Compensation shall be the fair market value of the part taken, determined as of the date of taking, plus damages to the remainder resulting from the taking and from the construction and use of the project as planned, less the value of any special benefit conferred on the remainder. General benefits shared with the community at large shall not be offset. Value shall be determined with reference to the highest and best use, which may include a use requiring a rezoning where the rezoning is reasonably probable.

sections.heading: RIDER 4 — RELOCATION AND BUSINESS LOSSES
sections.text: The Owner is entitled to actual and reasonable moving expenses, expenses of searching for a replacement site not exceeding $45,000, and reestablishment expenses. Loss of business profits and loss of goodwill are not compensable except to the extent expressly provided by statute. Payment of relocation benefits is not an offset against just compensation.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Indemnity
sections.text: Each party shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the other from all claims, damages and expenses, including reasonable attorney's fees, arising out of that party's use of the subject premises or breach of this instrument, except to the extent caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of the party seeking indemnity. This clause survives termination.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Governing Law
sections.text: This instrument shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Kestrel, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles. Any action arising out of or relating to this instrument shall be brought exclusively in the courts sitting in Pinecrest County, Kestrel, and each party consents to the personal jurisdiction of those courts.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Entire Agreement and Riders
sections.text: This instrument, together with the exhibits and riders attached and incorporated by reference, constitutes the entire agreement of the parties and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations and agreements, whether oral or written. In the event of a conflict between a printed provision and a rider, the rider shall control, the rider being the specifically negotiated expression of the parties' intent.
